Vanessa,

Thanks for sending over the DPA — quick follow-ups from our privacy team as they review cross-border exhibits. Two asks so we can complete our internal review today: 

1) Can you confirm which Redwood subprocessors have access to unredacted PII in transit vs. at rest, and whether any of those subprocessors store keys outside the EU for EU customer data?
2) We need a short wiring/dataflow diagram that highlights the boundary where egress is possible (even if routed through a proxy) and the associated KMS custody (who holds keys).

If you can include any existing KMS attestation or SOC2 artifact reference that would speed this along. We have a hard cutover for procurement approvals by COB today.

Appreciate it,

Lily Zhang
Data Privacy Manager — Medidata Therapeutics
Lily.Zhang@medidata.com

Subject: Re: Questions on DPA transfer annex + diagram

Lily — thanks for the clear asks. High level answers up front, and Marissa & Priyom are looping in the artifacts.

- Subprocessors with access to unredacted PII: our dedicated infra subprocessors (ObjectStoreCo, CDNPartner) do not retain unredacted PII; only compute and our KMS provider have transient access for decryption during inference. Persistent access is limited to our KMS provider for key escrow.
- KMS custody: keys for EU tenant data are customer-segregated; primary key material is managed by Redwood using the customer’s key in our KMS instance, and the KMS HSM is hosted in EU regions. No key material is exported to non-EU HSMs for EU-tagged tenants unless explicitly requested.

Artifacts attached: redwood-dataflow-v3.pdf (annotated wiring), kms-attestation-2028-03.pdf. Priyom — can you confirm the list of subprocessors and a one-line justification for each? Marissa — attaching a short privileged-access checklist (access-checklist-privileged-roles.xlsx) — please confirm the current role-owner mapping.

Next steps: if that covers it we can provide a short statement for your procurement and legal teams and link the Drive file for their records.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Enterprise GTM — Redwood Inference

Vanessa / Marissa — looped in Karthik and Grace for technical confirmation. Answers below in-line to map back to their asks; please paste into a short note for Lily/Legal Ops.

1) Subprocessor access profile (one-liners):
- ObjectStoreCo (EU region): object storage for artifact retention, encrypted at rest, no key material; access limited to storage API, objects are pseudonymized where possible.
- CDNPartner (global): caches encrypted assets only; does not hold keys and cannot serve decrypted PII content.
- InferencePoolOps (dedicated hosts): transient decryption in-memory for inference; KV cache is ephemeral and not persisted to disk.
- KMSProvider (EU-HSM): key escrow and rotation; HSMs located in Frankfurt and Amsterdam; customer keys are tenant-segregated.

2) Cross-border routing: Default routing for EU tenants keeps traffic in EU. In the annotated diagram we show the fallback path (edge -> compute in us-east) which only triggers for specified burst scenarios; that path requires an explicit routing policy and is logged for export approvals.

3) Evidence: attached KMS attestation covers key generation/rotation and HSM locality. I included a Drive link to the network egress rules and the redwood-dataflow-v3.pdf shows the exact boundary box for cross-border egress.

Action items for this thread (short):
- Marissa: confirm role-owner mapping and add one-sentence on offboarding verification (deadline: 15:00 PT).
- Karthik: confirm the fallback routing policy text we can share with procurement (deadline: 15:30 PT).
- Vanessa: if procurement/legal want a line-item for the contract annex we can draft it and sign off.

Thanks — Priyom

Lily / Marco / Legal Ops — attaching the artifacts requested and a short statement for procurement. Key points below and the Drive link includes the annotated diagram and a one-page export control note.

Short statement for procurement/legal: 
- Data residency and key custody: EU tenant data remains in EU by default. Tenant keys are resident in our EU KMS HSM cluster; no key material is exported outside the EU unless the customer explicitly requests cross-region key replication.
- Subprocessors: the only subprocessors that perform decryption for inference are InferencePoolOps (ephemeral compute) and KMSProvider (key custody). Storage and CDN partners do not hold plaintext PII.
- Egress fallback: cross-border fallback paths exist for capacity emergencies and require: (1) explicit routing policy, (2) logs retained for 3 years, (3) pre-approval by customer/legal.

Attachments: redwood-dataflow-v3.pdf (diagram, annotated boundary boxes), kms-attestation-2028-03.pdf (KMS HSM locality & attestation), access-checklist-privileged-roles.xlsx (current privileged-role owners + offboarding checklist).

If this addresses your procurement items we can sign the annex today. Happy to hop on a 15m call if Legal Ops want to walk through the diagram.

Regards,
